section_summary: This section continues a report on Allied surveillance of Japan’s April 1947 elections. It includes reporting forms, checklists, a surveillance map, and British Commonwealth operational instructions, followed by assessments of polling coverage and election publicity. The final pages describe party alignments, campaign issues, and policy platforms.

people.name: Timothy J. Ryan
people.role: Lieutenant colonel, Infantry; commanding officer of the Saitama Military Government Team

people.name: Shigeru Yoshida
people.role: Prime Minister, referred to through his cabinet

subfiles.title: Report form on surveillance of elections
subfiles.about: A model form records local election participation, candidates, surveillance, violations, and military government evaluations.
subfiles.summary: The form requests prefectural and large-city election statistics, details of polling and counting surveillance, reports of violations, campaign expenditures, and assessments by military government teams.

subfiles.title: Organization of Surveillance Teams
subfiles.about: The report explains staffing, geographic assignments, and coordination of election surveillance teams.
subfiles.summary: Three-person teams were assigned districts and maintained telephone contact with prefectural election offices.

subfiles.title: Kyushu Military Government Region Check List
subfiles.about: A preparatory checklist covers observer assignments, briefings, contacts, reporting, and communications.
subfiles.summary: Checks team readiness, polling assignments, interpreters, publicity, reporting requirements, and emergency contacts.

subfiles.title: Standard Surveillance Plan for Fukui Prefecture
subfiles.about: A map illustrates surveillance districts and polling places examined in Fukui Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Shows 25 districts and reports that teams examined 526 of 548 polling places on 25 April.

subfiles.title: British Commonwealth Occupation Force Operation for the April Election
subfiles.about: Operational instructions assign British Commonwealth personnel to pre-election, election-day, and post-election surveillance.
subfiles.summary: The order divides coverage between Chugoku and Shikoku, specifies interpreter and non-interpreter teams, and assigns polling-place observation and reporting duties. It also addresses transport, liaison with United States military government teams, correction of violations, and rapid reporting. Pages 7–8 and 11–12 contain substantially repeated text.

subfiles.title: Observing and Reporting
subfiles.about: The report compares the scale and results of election surveillance in 1946 and 1947.
subfiles.summary: Despite more polling places, fewer available personnel, and four election days, teams visited about half of polling places and 54 percent of counting stations at each 1947 election.

subfiles.title: Comparative Number and Disposition of Polling Places in Sapporo
subfiles.about: A figure compares polling-place distribution in Sapporo for the 1946 and 1947 elections.
subfiles.summary: Diagram of Sapporo polling places in the two elections.

subfiles.title: Polling Station Check List
subfiles.about: A form guides inspection of polling-place management, delays, complaints, and election-law violations.
subfiles.summary: Records visits, officials, watchers, police, irregularities, complaints, and corrective action.

subfiles.title: Ballot Counting Station Check List
subfiles.about: A form guides inspection of ballot-counting arrangements, observers, complaints, and violations.
subfiles.summary: Records station visits, management, watchers, counting methods, complaints, and corrective action.

subfiles.title: Roles of U.S. Army, BCOF, and U.S. Navy
subfiles.about: The report describes Allied units’ roles and experiences in election surveillance.
subfiles.summary: United States Army units carried the principal burden; British Commonwealth forces covered nine western prefectures, and Navy teams covered Yokosuka. The report describes extensive observation, minor violations corrected locally, and no irregularities observed in Yokosuka.

subfiles.title: Measures to Publicize Elections: Contents
subfiles.about: A divider lists the report’s categories of election publicity.
subfiles.summary: Lists occupation forces, radio, motion pictures, government agencies, and press.

subfiles.title: Measures to Publicize Elections: Occupation Forces
subfiles.doc_type: report section with reproduced public statements
subfiles.from: Occupation authorities; Timothy J. Ryan for the reproduced statements
subfiles.to: Japanese voters, including the people of Saitama
subfiles.about: Occupation authorities used press, film, radio, bulletins, and public meetings to encourage informed voting.
subfiles.summary: The section describes SCAP and military government voter education, including press conferences, a film, radio programs, bilingual bulletins, and community outreach. It reproduces two Saitama statements by Timothy J. Ryan urging genuine electoral competition and signed reports of election-law violations.

subfiles.title: Japanese Publicity
subfiles.about: The report surveys Japanese radio, film, government, and newspaper publicity surrounding the April elections.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasting authorities allocated candidate and party airtime and aired voter education messages; film companies and government agencies promoted participation. The press discussed turnout, campaign finance, party voting, the purge, and the results of the Councillors and Representatives elections. The report judges that post-election allegations of fraud and corruption were comparatively rare.

subfiles.title: Political and Campaign Issues: Contents
subfiles.about: A divider introduces political alignments, campaign issues, and party platforms.
subfiles.summary: Lists the three topics of the following report section.

subfiles.title: Political and Campaign Issues
subfiles.about: The report analyzes party realignments and the principal campaign issues and platforms of five major parties.
subfiles.summary: It traces the March 1947 party mergers and shifts in Diet strength, then outlines Liberal, Democratic, Social Democratic, People’s Cooperative, and Communist campaign positions. Major disputes concerned economic control, inflation, taxation, industry, agriculture, and labor. The section also summarizes broader platform differences before the detailed comparison table.

subfiles.title: The Platforms of the Five Major Parties
subfiles.about: A table compares the five major parties’ stated policies across several policy areas.
subfiles.summary: The table sets out Democratic, Liberal, Social Democratic, People’s Cooperative, and Communist proposals on administration, finance, industry, diplomacy, and food supply. It continues beyond page 41.
